Popular Safari extension StopTheMadness developer Jeff Johnson said that despite Apple's claim to review submissions, brazen rating scams keep slipping through the App Store.

He said he wasn't deliberately looking for scam apps on the App Store, but kept stumbling across them, and shared a recent example……

The App Store is a "safe and trusted place"

Apple takes a hardline stance on any antitrust measures involving third-party App Stores or iPhone sideloading, and usually only relents when legally compelled. Even so, Apple continues to defend its position.

The company claims all this is not about money, but about protecting iPhone users from malware. For example, Apple said last year that it had blocked more than US$9 billion in fraudulent transactions.

However, many developers question the claim that the App Store is a safe place, pointing to numerous scams involving millions of dollars. Just last month, Apple was sued by three customers who said their Bitcoin was stolen entirely by a fake wallet app.

App Store rating scams

App Store rating scams are a long-standing problem, with some companies even renting "iPhone farms" in mainland China to mass-download apps and leave five-star reviews.

Developer Jeff Johnson (best known for his StopTheMadness Safari extension) said he considered this latest App Store review fraud case to be "large-scale and obvious." The app in question is TabControl Extension.

He said when he stumbled across it, it was ranked 12th on the US Mac App Store paid Safari extension chart, and the screenshots were clearly AI-generated fake images.

Another thing worth noting is that those fake screenshots claim the app has a "perfect 5-star 4.9" rating, misleading people into thinking these are App Store user reviews……Using App Store screenshots to make false statements is a common scam tactic I've mentioned before. When a developer submits an app to the App Store, Apple reviews not only the app itself, but also the App Store listing and metadata, including screenshots. The claims in scam app screenshots are often absurd to the extreme, yet Apple still approves them……Apple claims the App Store can protect users from bad developers. If App Store review can't even catch this kind of thing, what's the point of reviewing? Frankly, App Store review doesn't need to be as detailed as what I do. A single screenshot claiming a "perfect 5-star 4.9" is itself a red flag. Apple has records of every rating and review in every country, and they know full well this is false advertising. I don't need to bloody download the app to know the developer is trying to scam users.

As he put it, if a developer is willing to use deceptive tactics to promote their app from the outset, you obviously wouldn't want to hand over your browsing data to them.

9to5Mac's view

Of course, completely eliminating all App Store scams is impossible, but fake reviews are extremely common, and cases like this should be obvious for Apple. How this extension got through review is baffling.

Apple should at least set up a mechanism that automatically subjects any rapidly rising app to stricter scrutiny, examining the app itself and the claims it makes.
